headline: Law requires the Interior Department to grant land access for utilities and roads to expand the Apex Industrial Park near North Las Vegas, Nevada.
what_it_does: The law directs the Interior Department to grant rights-of-way across federal land so North Las Vegas and the Apex Industrial Park Owners Association, along with Clark County, can connect power, water, gas, phone, rail, and highway lines to the Apex industrial park. It also requires, rather than just allows, Interior to grant other rights-of-way needed to develop the park as a heavy industrial zone. It keeps the transferred park lands permanently closed to claims and uses under public land laws, such as mineral leasing. Sales of rock, soil, and similar materials dug up during grading at the site are freed from the usual limits on amount and length for noncompetitive sales.

who_it_affects.how: The county must now be granted, rather than may be granted, rights-of-way needed to develop the industrial park.
The city will receive rights-of-way to connect utilities, rail, and roads to the park and to support its development.
The association will receive rights-of-way for utility and transportation connections and for developing the park.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners and developers at the Apex site
who_it_affects.how: They can sell mineral materials from grading work without the normal quantity and time limits on noncompetitive sales.
They cannot file claims or lease the transferred Apex lands under public land laws, since those lands stay withdrawn permanently.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 15, 2025; the summary does not give a separate effective date.
